Subject: Annual performance cycle: orchestration & comm pack (draft)

Team — kicking off a short thread to align on the 2025 review orchestration, comm drafts, and handoff to PeopleOps. I pulled together a lean pack (attached) that contains: the latest manager form (v3), a manager-facing comm draft, and a proposed cadence spreadsheet. High-level asks below.

Summary / goals
- Keep manager workload bounded (<2 hours per direct on average)
- Protect sensitive roles with silent routing and limited distribution lists
- Provide a single manager toolkit and a short one-pager for ICs

Proposed timeline (draft)
- Week 0 (Jul 7): Manager training & toolkit publish
- Week 1 (Jul 14): Manager review window opens (managers submit calibration notes by Jul 21)
- Week 2 (Jul 21–25): Calibration meetings; HR validations for sensitive roles
- Week 3 (Jul 28): Signoffs & final compensation inputs to Finance by Aug 1

Special handling (sensitive roles)
- Use separate distribution list: sensitive-review@redwood.com (HR + Legal + relevant manager)
- Manager packets redacted for peer reviewers; only HR sees full notes

Concrete asks for this thread
1) Marissa — read the manager comm draft and suggest edits for tone and length (attached).
2) Tessa — sanity-check the calibration week schedule vs. CS/Platform blackout dates (we should avoid product launches).
3) Laura — confirm legal needs for retention language and signoff owners for privileged roles.
4) Grace/Ellen — confirm PeopleOps can ingest v3 form and whether the HR vendor needs fields changed for our KMS/PII labeling.

Attachments: 2025-review-form-v3.docx, manager-comm-draft-2025.txt, timeline-cadence-v2.xlsx

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Engineering Managers
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — quick pass from me below. I kept comments inline in the manager-comm-draft but flag the main items here so they don't get lost: 

- Tone: shorten and lead with the single concrete action. Managers are triaged by priority; start with "what you need to do in 3 bullets."
- Calibration: recommend we front-load a short calibration rubric (1 page) to reduce back-and-forth in meetings.
- Sensitive roles: clarify the approval chain — suggest HR -> Legal -> Director rather than HR -> Director -> Legal (legal prefers to see before final signoff).
- Form: V3 looks good; propose adding a checkbox for "safety/data-sensitive" so the HR vendor can auto-route fields. Ellen — can the vendor support checkbox routing?

Small editorial suggestions on comm copy attached (manager-comm-draft-2025-edits.txt). I also trimmed the manager time estimate to 1.5 hours/direct where we can split pre-work into a short input form for ICs.

Minor: Can we avoid putting compensation timing into the initial comm? It raises queries from ICs before calibration is done. Suggest compensation notes go in a separate follow-up.

—Marissa
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference

Marcus / team — checked the proposed weeks against product/ops calendar: there are two launch freeze windows during Jul 20–24 and Aug 3–5 for Platform and Hosted Infra. Those overlap with calibration week as written and could block some managers. Proposed tweaks: 

- Shift calibration meetings earlier: Jul 15–18 (move manager window open one week earlier)
- OR split calibration across two half days (mornings only) Jul 21 and Jul 24 to avoid full-day conflicts

Either approach works; my preference is to move manager window one week earlier so calibration happens before those freeze windows. That yields a new timeline: manager training Jul 30? Wait that conflicts — see below adjusted calendar.

Adjusted timeline suggestion (compact)
- Week -2 (Jul 7): Final toolkit & manager quick training (30m live + recording)
- Week -1 (Jul 14): Manager window open (inputs due Jul 18)
- Calibration block (Jul 15–18): facilitated 90m sessions; HR handles sensitive role reviews in parallel
- Week 0 (Jul 21): Final signoffs and comp inputs to Finance by Jul 25

I attached a calendar view (timeline-cadence-v2.xlsx) with blocked times for calibration sessions and suggested facilitator assignments.

Also — agree with Marissa on keeping comp messaging out of the first comm. We should add an FAQ doc for managers about comp timing instead.

—Tessa

Redwood Inference

Thanks for the thoughtful pack. A few legal/retention notes and a go-forward ask: 

1) Retention language: we need explicit retention windows for manager notes and calibration artifacts. Proposed copy: "Manager notes and calibration records will be retained for 24 months for audit and compliance, then archived. Access will be restricted to HR and Legal for the first 12 months." Please slot this into the manager comm and the form.

2) Sensitive roles: legal wants the approval sequence to be HR review -> Legal review -> Director signoff for any redactions or role-specific exception language. That means Marissa/Ellen — factor in an extra 48 hours in the schedule for legal review on flagged items.

3) Data handling: the manager form must explicitly call out what PII may be entered and how it is stored (our KMS reference and vendor storage location). We're fine with a checkbox route but require a field that documents encrypted-at-rest location (vendor field).

Next steps (short)
- Marissa: finalize comm draft with my retention wording and remove comp timing from the initial notice.
- Tessa: please publish the revised calendar (move manager window to Jul 14–18 per your note) and add 48-hour legal buffer for flagged items.
- Marcus: once items above are in, route to PeopleOps and vendor; Ellen please confirm vendor can support checkbox-based routing and an encrypted location field.

I am good with the plan otherwise. Please keep the comm succinct and action-oriented.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel
Redwood Inference
